chunks: And a group informed us on the authority of Abu Muhammad Harun ibn Musa, who said: Abu Ali Muhammad ibn Himam (may Allah be pleased with him and satisfy him) informed me that Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Uthman al-Amari (may Allah sanctify his soul) called us before his death. We were the elite of the Shia and their senior members. He said to us: 'If the incident of death befalls me, the command is with Abu al-Qasim al-Husayn ibn Ruh al-Nuqbakhti. I have been ordered to place him in my position after me. So refer to him and rely on him in your affairs.'

key_terms.أَبُو الْقَاسِمِ الْحُسَيْنِ بْنِ رَوْحٍ: Abu al-Qasim al-Husayn ibn Ruh, a prominent deputy of the Imam
key_terms.النُّوبَخْتِيُّ: Al-Nuqbakhti, a nisba indicating origin from Nuqbakht
key_terms.وُجُوهَ الشِّيعَةِ: The elite/leading figures of the Shia

ai.seo_question: Who did Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Uthman appoint as his successor before his death?
ai.summary: This narration from the *Kitab al-Ghayba* underscores the institutional continuity of the Shia leadership during the Minor Occultation, where Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Uthman al-Amari, a prominent chief of the Shia, designates Abu al-Qasim al-Husayn ibn Ruh as his successor based on a specific command. It highlights the concept of *tawqif* (divine designation) within the scholarly hierarchy, ensuring that the community's religious and administrative affairs remained anchored to a trusted authority figure during the Imam's absence. This event serves as a critical precedent for the legitimacy of the *Fuqaha* and the structured transition of authority in Shia jurisprudence.
